definition: Beyond the Imitation Game Benchmark, a benchmark for measuring the performance of language models across a diverse set of tasks.
details: Beyond the Imitation Game Benchmark, a benchmark for measuring the performance of language models across a diverse set of tasks.

explainer.lead: BIG-Bench, short for Beyond the Imitation Game Benchmark, evaluates language models on a diverse set of tasks. It gives researchers and engineers a way to look beyond one narrow test and examine performance across many kinds of challenges.

tiers.eli5: BIG-Bench is like a school quiz with many different kinds of questions instead of just spelling or just maths. A language model tries the tasks, and its answers show what it can do well and where it struggles.
tiers.practitioner: Use BIG-Bench as an evaluation setting for comparing language-model behaviour across diverse tasks. Keep the task selection, prompts, and response-judging procedure consistent when comparing runs, and retain task-level results so that a summary does not hide weak areas. Do not assume a single accuracy or aggregation rule without defining one.
tiers.paperLevel: BIG-Bench is formally described as a benchmark that measures language-model performance over a diverse task set. Its evaluation object is task performance rather than one prescribed scalar formula; any aggregate score must therefore state its scoring and aggregation convention. Breadth of tasks does not imply uniform performance on every task or downstream application.

explainer.example: Suppose an illustrative evaluation contains two tasks, and a model produces one correct response and one incorrect response. Its record for this toy example is 1/2 = 50% correct; this demonstrates the arithmetic, not a prescribed BIG-Bench-wide scoring formula.

usedIn.name: Language model evaluation
usedIn.detail: Examines model performance across a diverse set of tasks rather than one narrow test.

usedIn.name: Language model comparison
usedIn.detail: Provides a shared benchmark setting for examining how different models handle the same evaluation tasks.

explainer.measures: BIG-Bench measures the performance of language models across a diverse set of tasks. Its focus is breadth of evaluated behaviour, not performance on just one application.
howScored: Present the language model with tasks from the benchmark.
Evaluate its responses and record performance across those tasks.
caveats: Do not assume that results on diverse tasks combine into one universal score.
Benchmark performance does not guarantee strong performance on every task or application.

diagram.caption: A language model attempts diverse tasks, and its responses are evaluated to measure performance.
